summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official: Ten-Minute Beginner Tutorial - Spaghetti Strap Dress ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will guide you through the steps to create a spaghetti strap dress using Marvelous Designer. Follow along to learn how to manipulate virtual models, create patterns, and sew them together for a complete look. ## Downloading the Virtual Model Please download the virtual model from the Femalemaster V2 file editor. ## Drawing Lines on the Virtual Model 1. Use the virtual model tool in the 3D toolbar to draw a line on the virtual model. 2. Press the **Ctrl** key to add a curve point. 3. When the line on the virtual model is completely closed, press the **Enter** key to remove the flat version. 4. Delete excess curve points and adjust the curve to make the line smoother. ## Aligning and Arranging the Model 1. Press **Ctrl D** to align the flat version with the seam line, and then **Shift F** to show the arrangement point. 2. Arrange the model around the virtual model. 3. Use the edit line virtual model tool to delete the line on the virtual model. 4. Extend the flat version to the body of the virtual model. ## Adjusting the Flat Version 1. After selecting the flat version, you can shrink it. 2. Move around, rotate, and adjust the curve of the plate according to the image of the virtual model. 3. Use the rectangle tool to create the back plate. 4. Adjust the width of the plate by moving the outside of the plate and the point of the straight line. 5. Use **Ctrl D** to align the plate with the sewing line. ## Moving and Adjusting Points 1. When moving the line or the point of the straight line, right-click to enter the number of movement in the spring. 2. Use the edit curve tool to adjust the curve of the plate. 3. Ensure that the length of the front and back plates is unified. 4. **Shift F** shows the arrangement of the plate. ## Sewing the Plates Together 1. You can adjust the position of the plate cover after selecting the plate you have arranged. 2. Use the vertical debut tool to sew the plates together. 3. Adjust the position of the plate with the tolerated evident solution tool. 4. Use the diagonal sewing tool to sew the plates together. 5. After sewing, you can move up or down the slice to attach the Juneziech paper pattern keyhole. ## Creating the Shoulder Strap 1. Select the top point on the outside line of the double-chip board with the same tool for the whole line, so that the board can be fixed to avoid falling. 2. After measuring the length of the seam line that the shoulder strap needs to be sewn, use the shoulder strap of the rectangular tool to draw the shoulder strap. 3. Press **Ctrl D** to align the board with the seam line. 4. **Shift F** to display the arrangement points around the virtual model and arrange the board. 5. Use the line sewing tool to sew the board together. ## Consistency in Sewing 1. To ensure that the direction of the seam line is consistent in the 3D window, select the free sewing tool in the 3D window for sewing. 2. The sewing tool selected in the 3D window can be used in the 2D and 3D windows at the same time. 3. Press the **W** key and click on the 3D window to add a pin. ## Adjusting Panels and Details 1. For too small boards, the number of grid spaces will be relatively small. Therefore, reduce the number of grid spaces with the example tool to make the board more detailed and smoother. 2. To separate the seam lines of the symmetrical boards, re-set the link relationship for the board. 3. Change the seam line and seam line to symmetrical boards. 4. Adjust the board to match, such as adding internal lines, but note that the seam line is not symmetrical. ## Finalizing the Design 1. Press the **W** key and click on the pin again to delete the pin or use **Ctrl W** to delete all pins. 2. Install hangarこん Mskew to thin the line map of the Baukstra. 3. Notice any gaps between the smart board and the virtual model, and set the surface of the virtual model as 0. ## Fixing and Adjusting Straps 1. Use the fixed needle tool to fix the strap. 2. After selecting the previous version, use 100% elasticity to maintain the length of the original line. 3. Use the edit curve point tool to adjust the curve. Align points of the inner line separately to the outer line of the version. 4. If the strap is too short, lengthen it by moving the curve point with the edit curve point tool. ## Applying Fabric and Adjusting Details 1. Apply a new fabric to the strap, such as trim foot grain leather, and increase friction and inner damping. 2. To prevent the strap from being stretched or lowered, maintain the shape of the original version for better adjustment. 3. If there are wrinkles on the back panel, narrow the panel a little. 4. Adjust the position and size of the strap as needed. ## Creating the River Side 1. Copy the front panel and reset the 3D arrangement position. 2. Choose the line and use the panel to expand the outer line. 3. If you change the side angle to Extend and select the inner line, it will expand along the side of the curve while creating the inner line in the original position. 4. Select and cut off the inner line, and delete excess panels and curve points. ## Final Adjustments 1. Use the trim line tool to adjust the curve. Ensure the width from the top to the bottom of the river side is gradually increased. 2. The river side should be wider than the front and back panels to avoid wrinkles. 3. Use the trim line tool or the free trim tool to trim the panels. 4. To avoid simulation instability, freeze the panels of the skirt. ## Symmetric Adjustments 1. Use the side to add the side of the river side to the seam line. 2. Hold down the Floral fork key to adjust the tip of the river side. ## Completing the Dress 1. To bring the skirt to shorts, move the skirt and press sec. 2. Use the free sewing tool to sew the river side and the skirt together. 3. Press **Shift C** to display the hidden panels. 4. Select the cold-wet panel and set its layer to 1. This will automatically identify which panel is on the outside and which is on the inside. 5. After activating, slice the panel to complete the dress. ## Finalizing the Belt 1. After sewing the back of the river side, use the square tool to make the belt. 2. **Shift F** to display the arrangement points and arrangement panels. 3. In the property editor, adjust the arrangement position of the panel. 4. For belt application, set the layer to 1, as the belt should be on the outer layer of the skirt. 5. Use the selection grid tool to select the position of the insertion. ## Component Adjustment 1. In the 3D window, use the positioning ball to drag the insertion part out. 2. After the simulation is stable, reset the layer. 3. Before simulation, replace the belt fabric with trim foot green leather to facilitate stretching and deformation. 4. Reduce the tail to green, and tighten the belt by 50%. ## Adding Hardware 1. Insert a bag from the Hardware and Trims Greater Than Ribbon file. 2. Click the slide icon in the upper right corner to adjust the size of the component. 3. Note that each component has a corresponding weight; adjust it in the attribute editor. 4. Reduce the particle diameter to achieve more detailed fold details. ## Conclusion Congratulations! You have completed the spaghetti strap dress tutorial in Marvelous Designer. Use these techniques to further explore your creativity and develop more complex designs. ```
